method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center' (published 29 September 2020), 25 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC9536714). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614) 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement' (published 22 August 2025), 10 claims; LICENCE: Publisher version CC BY 4.0 (Unpaywall); the PMC author manuscript read here carries the NIH statement 'available for text mining ... consistent with the principles of fair use' (read at NCBI efetch PMC JATS XML <permissions> for PMC13537435 (Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500); publisher licence per Unpaywall record for 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, a 2025 JACC: Heart Failure position statement on antibody-mediated rejection (AMR); S1 claims and anchors are unchanged. S2 shares one author (Kobashigawa) with S1, so the two are not fully independent. On 2026-09-24 the ISHLT 2022 guideline (DOI 10.1016/j.healun.2022.10.015; Unpaywall lists it as free to read at jhltonline.org) was retried: jhltonline.org and sciencedirect.com both returned Cloudflare challenges (HTTP 403) and the Elsevier text-mining API needs a key; the ESC-HFA 2026 heart transplantation consensus (DOI 10.1093/ejhf/xuag051) has no open copy (Unpaywall: closed). Neither was bypassed. The 2022 AST/ACCP/ASHP maintenance immunosuppression consensus (Pharmacotherapy) is closed access.

claims.claim: **Rejection risk is greatest soon after implantation and falls over time,** so immunosuppression is most intense straight after surgery and is stepped down over the first year to the lowest maintenance level that still prevents rejection and limits toxicity.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prefer low doses of several drugs with non-overlapping toxicities** to high doses of fewer; too much immunosuppression brings infection and cancer.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 50% of heart transplant recipients get induction.** The main reason is antibody sensitisation (risk of hyperacute rejection); others are multi-organ transplant and renal sparing, to delay the calcineurin inhibitor (CNI).
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **This centre prefers rabbit anti-thymocyte globulin (rATG) over basiliximab** for efficacy, and considers it when panel reactive antibody exceeds 10%: 1.5 mg/kg daily for 5 days from the day of surgery.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Maintenance usually pairs a CNI (tacrolimus or ciclosporin) with either an antimetabolite (mycophenolate mofetil, enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium or azathioprine) or a proliferation signal inhibitor (sirolimus or everolimus).**
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CNIs remain the backbone.** The centre starts triple therapy: tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and a corticosteroid (IV methylprednisolone, then oral prednisone).
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tacrolimus trough targets (this centre):** first month 10–15 ng/mL; second and third months 8–12 ng/mL; after the third month 5–10 ng/mL.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mycophenolate mofetil is dosed to tolerance (up to 1,500 mg twice daily) without routine levels;** gastrointestinal upset and cytopenias usually limit the dose.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid everolimus or sirolimus in the first 6 months** (wound dehiscence, poor healing, added CNI nephrotoxicity). Active fungal infection or past DVT/PE usually rules them out unless long-term anticoagulant or antifungal cover is sorted.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Best candidates to switch mycophenolate to a PSI:** treated rejection, new donor-specific antibodies, CMV mismatch or infection, malignancy, or cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Check proteinuria, lipids and glucose before starting and during treatment.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Steroid weaning in lower-risk recipients:** prednisone 10 mg daily by 3 months and 5 mg by 6 months, then down by 1 mg a month to stop by twelve months if graft function is normal, there has been no treated rejection or DSA, and adherence is good.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Keep prednisone 5 mg daily long term** after multi-organ transplant, and when sarcoidosis or giant cell myocarditis caused the cardiomyopathy.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney impairment:** minimise the CNI when it is mild (creatinine 1.8–2.2 mg/dL); withdraw it when moderate (creatinine >2.0–2.5 mg/dL), but only after 6 months and not during steroid weaning, or with past PSI intolerance, LV dysfunction, humoral rejection or cellular rejection above 2R.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Switching to a CNI-free regimen:** continue mycophenolate, halve the CNI and start the PSI, keeping low-dose CNI until PSI troughs are at target: sirolimus 4–8 ng/mL, everolimus 3–8 ng/mL.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 20% cannot tolerate a PSI.** Fatigue and fluid retention are commonest; others are fungal infection, pneumonitis, venous thromboembolism, high triglycerides, mouth ulcers, cytopenias and acute kidney injury. Review within 4 weeks of switching.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First-year prophylaxis (this centre):** clotrimazole troches for 3 months against thrush; valganciclovir (renally dosed) for 1 year if CMV donor-positive/recipient-negative, otherwise 6 months; co-trimoxazole for 1 year against Pneumocystis, toxoplasma and Nocardia.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Keeping CNI levels on target is critical.** Recheck bloods a week after any CNI dose change; check CNI troughs twice weekly in the first month and weekly in the second.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Low troughs have many causes:** missed doses, side effects or cost, malabsorption, altered cytochrome P450 metabolism, drug or food interactions, infection, cytopenias, or dose cuts for intolerance.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surveillance biopsy in year one:** weekly in month 1, fortnightly in month 2, monthly for months 3 to 6, then every other month to 12 months. Test for donor-specific antibodies at months 1, 3 and 6, then 6-monthly. Low-risk patients may use blood gene-expression profiling instead of some biopsies.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rejection can be silent.** Clues: new LV hypertrophy (oedema), new systolic dysfunction early after transplant, low-voltage ECG, raised BNP or troponin. Symptoms: breathlessness, orthopnoea, PND, a return of pre-transplant symptoms, or atrial fibrillation or flutter.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The transplanted heart is very sensitive to adenosine:** halve the dose to 3 mg, with continuous ECG monitoring, to avoid prolonged heart block. Use IV beta-blockers cautiously early on; amiodarone is acceptable with care.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biopsy when rejection is suspected.** If the biopsy is normal but there is graft dysfunction with heart failure, consider biopsy-negative rejection and cardiac MRI or molecular testing.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Symptomatic rejection (this centre):** IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for 3 days, then rATG for 3 to 7 days (usually 5). If donor-specific antibodies are present, add IVIG 1 g/kg daily for 2 days (maximum total 140 g). Repeat HLA antibody testing at the time of rejection.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cardiogenic shock from rejection** may need pulmonary artery catheter guidance, inotropes, an intra-aortic balloon pump, and early VA ECMO; ECMO started after cardiac arrest does poorly.
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrent rejection:** photopheresis may be considered. Re-transplant is generally contraindicated within 6 months of treated rejection (hyperacute rejection risk).
claims.locator: Youn JC, Chang DH, Dilibero D, Patel JK, Kobashigawa JA, International Journal of Heart Failure, 'Heart Transplant Immunosuppression Strategies at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center', published 29 September 2020, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9536714/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **How AMR happens:** donor-specific antibodies (DSA) bind donor HLA on the graft's vascular endothelium and switch on complement. Preformed high-titre DSA can cause hyperacute rejection; de novo DSA, usually against HLA class II, form after transplant. S2 suggests treating HLA DSA plus graft dysfunction as equivalent to AMR.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **AMR risk factors:** pre-transplant sensitisation, a positive flow-cytometric crossmatch, de novo DSA (class II above all) and too little immunosuppression. **Screen for de novo DSA at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, then every year;** whether to treat DSA without graft dysfunction or with a normal biopsy is not settled.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Donor-derived cell-free DNA** has a negative predictive value above 98%, allowing fewer biopsies; levels run 5 to 11 times higher in AMR than in cellular rejection and can rise about 3 months before biopsy diagnosis, but the test cannot tell the two apart.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Steroids first:** high-dose IV methylprednisolone and then a taper, used as part of a combination because steroids do not act on antibody production. During pulse and prolonged high-dose steroids, give prophylaxis for Pneumocystis, CMV and oral thrush.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Plasmapheresis and IVIG:** plasmapheresis removes DSA quickly, often every other day for 5 sessions, but antibodies rebound, so B-cell or plasma-cell therapy is added. IVIG is typically 2 g/kg in total, split across the plasmapheresis sessions (split dosing matters when graft function is poor); it can cause infusion reactions, aseptic meningitis and thrombosis.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Anti-thymocyte globulin for severe AMR or marked graft dysfunction:** usually 1.5 mg/kg IV once a day, 3–5 doses in all, with premedication; dosing can be guided by a CD3 count below 200–300 cells, and opportunistic-infection prophylaxis is advised.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Eculizumab (C5 complement inhibitor)** for severe, complement-active (C4d-positive) AMR: typically 900 mg weekly for at most 8 weeks, supported only by case series. Meningococcal vaccination before treatment and penicillin VK prophylaxis are mandatory.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Preventing antibody rebound:** rituximab clears circulating B cells for 6–12 months but leaves plasma cells producing DSA; bortezomib and carfilzomib deplete plasma cells. Bortezomib's main harm is peripheral neuropathy; carfilzomib has been linked to acute kidney injury and heart failure, reported in 67%.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Strengthen maintenance after AMR:** move ciclosporin to tacrolimus and azathioprine to mycophenolate, raise doses or trough targets, restart low-dose prednisone if it was weaned, or switch mycophenolate to an mTOR inhibitor.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **About 1 in 3 have chronic or recurrent AMR,** with more allograft vasculopathy and lower survival. Through the first year after treatment, monitor at set intervals with dd-cfDNA (with or without biopsy), echocardiography, DSA testing and/or intragraft gene expression.
claims.locator: Mehta A, DeFilippis EM, Stehlik J, Jackson AM, Kobashigawa JA, Shah P, JACC: Heart Failure 13(10):102614 (doi 10.1016/j.jchf.2025.102614), 'Contemporary Antibody-Mediated Rejection in Heart Transplantation: JACC: Heart Failure Position Statement', published 22 August 2025, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13537435/, retrieved 2026-09-24
